jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. You learn whatever domain each one lives in and build the thing that tests it: the prototype, the test article, the demonstration. Analysis gets a concept to the point where it is worth building; building it is how we find out. You are the technical authority for the concepts you own: you set the approach, review the work, and decide, on the evidence, which concepts continue and which stop. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As a Discovery Engineer you pick up a concept nobody has proven, learn whatever domain it lives in, build the analysis or prototype that tests it, and get to an answer. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, do the work, check it, and reach a solution. You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of getting engaged in problems across different areas, being analytic, testing new concepts, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first. Underpinning these diverse robotic fleets is our DeviceOS team , which engineers the unified, highly reliable operating system and hardware-enablement platform that powers all of Anduril's autonomous assets. jobs.description_text: Anduril Maritime builds autonomous underwater/surface vehicles: autonomy computers running control and mission logic, payload computers driving sonar and other sensors, surface integration units, and ground control stations. We're past the "does it work in the lab" phase - vehicles are in the field, and field vehicles find bugs the lab never does. We need someone whose job, starting day one, is to pick up those bugs and actually close them: reproduce it, find the real cause, fix it, ship it, tell the team what happened. To be clear about what this isn't: it's not a ticket-triage-and-forward job, and it's not "junior dev does the boring work while senior devs build features." You'll be shipping real fixes in the real codebase. You're just entering the codebase through "this broke on a vehicle" instead of "here's a clean feature spec." Once you've built up cross-subsystem fluency - which this role forces faster than sitting in one subsystem ever would - you move into owning subsystems and roadmap work like anyone else. What you'll actually be doing Take a field-reported anomaly (sensor stopped publishing, mission faulted mid-track, data stream drifted for no obvious reason) and figure out what subsystem it's actually in - not just where it was reported. jobs.department: Hardware Platform : Hardware Engineering Services : Dev Fabrication
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM The Development Fabrication team within Mechanical Services turns early engineering concepts into physical hardware for some of Anduril’s highest-priority programs. This is not a production line. Our team builds low-volume, high-complexity prototype hardware — custom chassis, structural frames, fixtures, test articles, and complex weldments — often while designs are still evolving. Fabricators work directly with design engineers to determine how hardware should actually be built, identify problems before they reach integration, and rapidly turn ideas into functional hardware. Every build is different. The drawings may change. The material may fight you. A design that works perfectly in CAD may not work on the shop floor. Our job is to figure it out — quickly, safely, and correctly. The result is a highly collaborative prototype environment where experienced fabricators are trusted for their judgment, not simply handed a print and told to weld. ABOUT THE JOB As a Senior Development Fabrication Technician, you will take prototype hardware from drawing to finished assembly . You’ll plan the build, select the right fabrication approach, lay out and fit components, weld and machine hardware, design fixtures, inspect your work, and solve problems as they emerge. You will work directly with engineers when drawings are incomplete, tolerances create problems, or a design simply isn’t practical to manufacture.
